messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from today's multi-region discussion. I sketched a lightweight 'consent checkpoint' inside the edge proxy that can short-circuit cross-region KV swaps for most reads. Thinking this reduces handoff churn while respecting residency flags.

kai: Can you outline the invariants it must preserve? main worry is stale reads when we short-circuit.

maria: Invariants: 1) never return data that violates tenant residency. 2) if checkpoint says 'local-ok' we serve from local cache. 3) otherwise we escalate to the normal cross-region arbitration.

sanjay: Sounds good. For reads, we can attach a 2-bit vector: {consent_granted, fresh_ok}. Proxy checks vector before deciding. cheap to store in memcache.

maria: Exactly. To avoid additional round trips, the vector would be computed at write time and piggybacked on the write replication headers.

ana: small nit: spelling — my name is ana (no extra n). also how does this work with active/active when two regions think local-ok? race?

kai: Race is a core problem. Proposal: consent checkpoint only allows local reads for keys with an append-only write token or when recent replication ACKs are present. If replication lag > threshold, checkpoint declines.

leo: Operationally, we need an operator-visible metric: checkpoint_declines_by_reason. otherwise we'll blind-deploy.

maria: Agreed. Also proposing a soft-fence mode for cutovers: checkpoint can be toggled per-tenant to 'strict' during a migration window via the control plane. That avoids global rollbacks.

devon: How about a tiny API shim for clients so they can ask for 'consent-liveness' before doing heavy reads? e.g., `GET /consent/:tenant/:key?probe=true` returning {consent:true, ts:165...}.

sanjay: That would help debugging. We should supply an idempotent probe that doesn't count towards cost quotas.

kai: Implementation sketch in proxy config (pseudo):
```
consent_checkpoint: true
consent_ttl_ms: 2000
consent_replication_ack_threshold_ms: 500
consent_modes: { normal: accept_if_acked, strict: reject_if_unacked }
```

maria: Nice. Also thinking about a checksum reconciliation job for KV caches to detect drift. It runs nightly and emits diffs to the operator dashboard. If drift > X% for a tenant, we auto-escalate to strict mode.

leo: What about privacy/legal audits? We must ensure the checkpoint logs nothing PII and that the reconcile diffs are only aggregate hashes.

maria: Yes — reconcile outputs will be HMACed key prefixes + counts only. No raw values.

devon: Rollout plan: 1) feature-flag in staging for 5% traffic 2) enable probes 3) collect checkpoint_declines_by_reason + reconcile_drift 4) expand.

kai: Suggest we also add a fallback tracer header so client requests get a short id that surfaces path taken (proxy-checkpoint/local-cache/cross-escrow). Helps postmortems.

maria: Good call. Format: `X-Rw-Trace: cp=accept,src=local,lat=12ms` (short).

deploy-bot: CI pipeline: consent-checkpoint proxy changes merged to feature branch. Unit tests: 134 passed, 2 flaky. Canary job queued.

ana: Will ops need new runbooks? I can start a runbook draft: how to flip tenant to strict, how to interpret decline metrics, how to escalate when reconcile drift spikes.

maria: Please do. Also add runbook steps for performing a manual checksum resync for a tenant (force rehydrate from canonical store).

leo: I'll wire up the dashboard panels and alert: reconcile_drift > 0.5% in 1h -> pager to eng-ops.

sanjay: One more edge: embeddings/large-value objects. Checkpoint should always decline for values > 64KB and send them to arbitration to avoid partial reads.

maria: Good constraint. I'll add that to the proto and then we can cut a short RFC note describing operator impacts.

kai: TL;DR: consent checkpoint = proxy-level fast-path for residency-safe reads, requires replication ACK heuristics + size/age gates, operator metrics + reconcile job, and per-tenant strict toggle for migrations.

devon: :thumbsup: When you have the RFC note, ping eng-arch and I'll schedule a 30m sync with SRE and Legal for audit signoff.

maria: Will do. Thanks everyone.
